newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas mostly stable but 97/98 contango narrows.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas mostly stable but 97/98 contango narrows.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices were largely unchanged on Monday in quiet trade, dealers said.

The market was extremely quiet until around 1530 GMT, a trader said, when activity picked up slightly. One company traded a 1997 gas year at 13 pence a therm, and also traded each quarter separately at prices which averaged out at 13 pence. The individual quarters were done at 13.30 pence (Q4), 16.95 pence (Q1), 11.375 pence (Q2) and 10.375 pence (Q3).

Apart from these trades, a 1998 gas year was done at 13.25 pence a therm. "The only real softening is in gas year 1998," a trader said. "The contango (between the 97 year and the 98 year) at 0.25 pence is the lowest it's been. This is predominantly due to an aggressive seller rather than any change in fundamentals," he added.

The only other period to see much activity was in the prompt market. A within day deal for a million therms was done at Bacton at 9.65 pence a therm. The buyer said that while it was common to buy that volume in a single day, it was "not that often" that it was done in a single trade as few sellers were able to offer such a large volume.

A seller at St Fergus said there was some buying interest for Q1 gas, but the bid came no higher than 16.30 pence and the offer stuck at 16.45 pence, so no trade was concluded. In view of the NBP trade in Q1 at 16.95 pence, the seller agreed that the offer prices was on the high side.
August was slightly softer, with trade done at 9.45 pence a therm for the whole month, but otherwise prices were mostly unchanged, traders said.
While the OTC market was quiet, the futures market was completely untraded for the first time since July 8.
